evidence.name: VehiclePhysicsTimeStep

function_ir.summary: Per-frame vehicle physics timestep. Computes frame delta time, decodes the packed input packet (orientation, steering, velocity, subsystem bits) via a set of bitfield/short-vector helpers, transforms state into the vehicle struct, runs per-wheel suspension updates, and dispatches mode-specific state machines (mode 2 = full vehicle setup copy + subsystem loop; mode 3 = vibration + subsystem loop). Ends by deriving braking/audio/bit flags from the packet and updating effect fields.

operations.description: Compute frame delta time v36 = a3 - lastTime (this+0x48B8), then store the new timestamp a3 into this+0x48B8.
Decode the packed orientation/input packet at a2+8 into component vectors v37 and v39 via ArithmeticComparison_2420.
Build a 3x3 rotation matrix v43 from Euler angles v39 via EulerToRotationMatrix.
Transform orientation components v37 by the rotation matrix v43 via F_3x3MatrixTransform.
Extract the steering float from the packed bitfield at a2+8 via BitfieldToFloatConversion into v30.
Clamp steering v30 to the range [-1.0, 1.0] and store the clamped value into this+0x1040.
Compute steering factor v35 = this+0x1044 * clamped steering v30.

For each wheel 0..3: unpack per-wheel data via sub_4B28F0 into v32 and v41[i]; accumulate v34 = v36 * wheelComponent + wheel accumulator at this+0x8C0 (stride 74 dwords); call SuspensionParamUpdate with steering factor v35 for wheels 0/1 and 0.0 for wheels 2/3.
Unpack velocity from the packed short vector at a2+8 into v38 via ShortVectorToFloatWithScale.
Truncate packed float data at a2+8 into v42 via FloatTruncation.
Unpack short-vector data at a2+8 into raw bytes v40 via ShortToFloatVectorUnpack.
Extract scaled bitfield value v31 from a2+8 via BitfieldExtractScale.
Compute speed scalar v32 from a2+8 via ShortComputation_29f0.
Write recovered orientation state: this+0xA4 = speed scalar v32; this+0x1C/0x20/0x24 = v37[0..2].
Copy the 36-byte rotation matrix v43 into the vehicle's orientation storage at this+52 (qmemcpy 0x24 bytes).
Write velocity vector v38 into this+0x58/0x5C/0x60.
Write steering scale v31 into this+0xA0.
Set byte this+0x1069 = (a2+52 bit 0x80) != 0.
Branch on vehicle mode v15 = this+0x32C8: if 2, run the full setup-data path; else if 3, run the vibration path.
Mode 2: store clamped steering v30 into this+0x3580.
Mode 2: BitfieldExtract(a2+8) into v16, then VehicleSetupDataCopy(v37, v39, v43, v38, v42, v40, v16) and EffectParameterSetter(v31, 0.5, v32) to copy setup data into the vehicle.
Mode 2: store per-wheel force values v41[i] into this+0x35BC + i*62 dwords for all 4 wheels.
Mode 2: compute v20 = a3 - lastSetupTime (this+0x48B4) and set byte this+0x344C = (a2+56 < 0).
Mode 2: if fabs(v20) > 15.0, refresh this+0x48B4 = a3 and drive all 14 subsystem state machines: BitTest(a2+8, i) then SubsystemStateMachine(i, bit).
Mode 3: run MatrixVectorSetup(v43, v40), drive all 4 VibrationStateMachine(j, v41[j]), then all 14 subsystem state machines via BitTest(a2+8, k) + SubsystemStateMachine(k, bit).
Compute braking flag v26 = (a2+56 bit 0x8000000) != 0.
If stored byte this+0x105D differs from v26, update this+0x105D and call AudioSoundEffectController(this+0x1054) to refresh the audio/render state on change.
Compute v27 = (a2+56 bit 0x4000000) != 0; write this+0x1065 = v27 and set this+0x3584 to 1.0 when v27 is set, else 0.
Set byte this+0x1067 = (a2+56 bit 0x2000000) != 0.
Compute v28 via ShortComputation_2b00(a2+8) and pass it to PropertySetter (both helpers named only in the raw source; no packet callee entries).
Write word this+0x48B0 = BitfieldExtract_2b80(a2+8).
Set byte this+0x4024 = (a2+59 bit 1).
Write float this+0x4028 = BitfieldExtractionWithScale(a2+8).

vehicle.speed = speed; vehicle.ori[0..2] = ori; copy rot -> vehicle+52;
unresolved: Raw source calls ShortComputation_2b00, PropertySetter, BitfieldExtract_2b80 and BitfieldExtractionWithScale, but the packet lists no callee entries (and therefore no addresses) for them; they are recorded as named calls with source:raw evidence only.

Global reads flt_59E43C / flt_59E670 / flt_59E8D8 are reported by the packet but no use is visible in the recovered raw source; they are likely consumed by inlined helper code not surfaced by the decompiler.
